# Retrospective: PR 12833

## Worked

Verified new Fable High and Astra Xhigh sessions received equivalent neutral scope and separate artifact directories. Both independently executed useful checks without peer conclusions. Real pacman in synthetic databases complemented source/test review, and Fable's isolated transactions distinguished silent removal from dependency refusal. Baseline negative controls showed the new tests reject the old policy; a diagnostic mutation yielded one concrete optional improvement.

## Friction and improvements

AUR access required a saved GitHub mirror rather than the blocked official endpoint. The custom-root pacman owner lookup needed a documented path-routing adapter. Future package reviews can reuse this pattern, including package-state postconditions rather than relying only on command logs. An unsealed prototype was preserved but not treated as evidence of record.

The reviewer proposed hypothetical future dependency advice and a pre-existing migration hypothesis. Synthesis correctly kept these local rather than padding a clean public production assessment. Documentation nuance was folded into the baseline/head comparison.

## Tool and resource notes

No confirmed tool bugs. No desktop slot or Omadev session needed. Review.py seals passed for all four bundles. Private runtimes/homes were ephemeral; no persistent test services or host configuration changes. Clean source worktrees and historical artifacts remain preserved. No pages opened and no comments posted by the coordinator.

## Carry forward

Use real package-manager transactions with synthetic local packages when conflict/dependency behavior matters. Keep hardware claims separate from package postconditions. Preserve independent reviewer session identities, exact editorial hashes and brief public scope qualifiers.
comment:
**Verified:** No production issue found in the package-selection scope at `9141da7848be`. Nonstock library owners skip `libfprint-git`; stock, fresh and existing-git installation behavior is preserved.

Real pacman transactions with synthetic packages produced this baseline/head comparison:

| Starting TOD state | Baseline | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No package depends on the TOD fork | Removes the fork noninteractively | Keeps the fork; installs `fprintd usbutils` |
| Vendor package depends on `libfprint-tod` | Refuses removal and aborts setup | Keeps both packages; installs missing tools |
| Same stack with both tools installed | Attempts the conflicting transaction | Skips installation; reaches enrollment |

Thus the baseline symptom can be either driver removal or a dependency-check failure, depending on the installed vendor package.

The nine package tests pass, and the updated suite rejects baseline code at the first TOD case. **Optional test improvement:** All nine also pass a diagnostic mutation replacing ownership lookup with a hardcoded `libfprint-tod` presence check. Adding a case with `LIBFPRINT_OWNER=libfprint-tod-git` and `INSTALLED=libfprint-tod-git`, checked with `assert_keeps_driver`, passes on this PR and rejects that mutation, protecting the intended package-name independence.
